Marker is retained. Finish rotating it vertical and align above the centered holder, keeping both EE links on their respective sides.
The wrists contacted above the cup. Separate them and lower the upright holder to prepare a less obstructive side grasp; retain the marker.
Replan the rejected separation with smaller right-arm increments, withdrawing the left wrist first.

Close the left grasp on the aligned pen and the right grasp around the upright cup sides, keeping its opening unobstructed.

Raise the side-held cup and align the upright retained pen above its opening, keeping wrist links separated.

One pen remains visibly seated. Move the empty left gripper toward the other yellow-and-black pen, turning downward above it.
Align the downward left grasp with the remaining yellow pen and descend above its shaft; keep the filled holder steady.
Correct the small wrist-image lateral offset, lower around the second pen shaft, and close while stabilizing the holder.
Lift the second pen clear of the table and rotate it toward vertical while approaching the held cup.
Finish turning the retained second pen vertical and position its lower end above the cup opening before descending.
Lower the second pen through the cup opening, holding its orientation and keeping the right-hand side grasp steady.

Move toward the nearer blue marker and orient the open left gripper for a top grasp; the cup stays upright in the right hand.
Complete downward orientation over the nearer blue marker and approach from above; the dropped yellow pen is visible on the table for later recovery.

Lift the closed marker grasp and begin turning it upright while retreating from the reach limit; verify retention in RGB.

Finish uprighting the marker and align its lower end above the open portion of the cup, leaving the seated pen undisturbed.

Inspect farther left where the dropped yellow pen was last visible, keeping the open gripper above the table and the cup fixed.
Inspect the near-left table edge where the yellow pen disappeared from the head view, with the gripper safely elevated.

Advance toward the far marker at a shallow angle, monitoring reach and keeping the right-hand holder stationary.
Use smaller forward increments and a shallower wrist angle toward the remaining marker, without forcing full extension.
Flatten the approach and lower rather than extending farther, aiming to reach the marker with the fingers while preserving arm reach margin.
Back off the table contact and level both fingers before any further approach to the far marker.
Roll the open left jaws to approach across the marker thickness rather than its full length, staying short of the reach limit.
Finish the vertical-jaw roll and approach the marker edge in small increments, aiming to slip the lower finger beneath its side.
Back away from the guarded far reach rather than force extension. Lower the upright holder toward the table with its two retained items.

Lift the recovered pen clear before rotating its upper end upright and bringing it toward the left-held cup.

Raise the recovered pen with no rotation to establish clear retention before turning it upright, leaving the cup fixed.
